# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

I read the code only. No live check was run, because no URL was given. The results below are read from code, not measured on a running site.

## Code score: 70/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16 ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. High = (16 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 70.

The site is a small Next.js App Router project with 5 routes, and I sampled all of them. The basics are mostly in place: `robots.txt` is valid, the nav uses plain links, and most content is rendered on the server. The score loses points for four reasons:
- There is no `Sitemap:` line in `robots.txt`.
- The `<html>` tag has no `lang`.
- `/pricing` is marked `noindex` while it sits in your sitemap and nav.
- `/blog` loads its posts only in the browser.

No score cap applied, because not every route is `noindex`.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point `robots.txt` at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** Crawlers find your list of pages through a `Sitemap:` line in `robots.txt`. Without it they have to guess where the list is.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-5`
- **What the code says:** the file contains only `User-agent: *`, `Allow: /`, `User-agent: GPTBot` and `Disallow: /`. It has no `Sitemap:` line, although `public/sitemap.xml` exists.
- **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Score after this:** 18 ÷ 23 = 78.

### 2. Set the page language on the root `<html>`
- **Why it matters:** The `lang` attribute tells machines and screen readers which language the pages are in. It is missing on every page.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small. Change it to `<html lang="en">`, which matches `site.language` in `geo.config.json`.
- **Score after this:** 18 ÷ 23 = 78. Doing items 1 and 2 together gives 20 ÷ 23 = 87.

### 3. Decide whether `/pricing` should be indexed, and remove `noindex` if so
- **Why it matters:** Pricing is in your sitemap and main nav, but it tells search engines to stay away. Its canonical link also points at a page marked `noindex`.
- **Where:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`
- **Size:** Small. If the `noindex` is intentional, remove `/pricing` from `public/sitemap.xml` and the nav instead.
- **Score after this:** removing `noindex` fixes both GEO-014 and GEO-015 for this route, giving 17.25 ÷ 23 = 75.

Next in line: `/docs` and `/blog` have no canonical link, and `/blog` fetches its posts in the browser (`app/blog/page.tsx:7-9`).

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: plain text, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` allows all. `GPTBot` is blocked (line 5), which matches your policy of blocking training crawlers and isn't scored. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` is `noindex`. 3 of 4 routes clear. `/thank-you` is `noindex` on purpose and isn't listed, so it isn't counted. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your own domain | Problem | Not run | `/` is clear. `/pricing` points its canonical at a `noindex` page. `/docs` and `/blog` have none. 1 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:1` is `'use client'`, and lines 7-9 fetch posts in `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes clear. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and is complete | Not applicable | Not run | No `application/ld+json` found |
| GEO-011 | Valid sitemap that `robots.txt` points to | Problem | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, but `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line (site-wide). The sitemap also lists the `noindex` `/pricing` (line 4). |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html `lang` | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` has `<html>` with no `lang`. Titles and descriptions are present on every route. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes reachable through server-rendered links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` has plain `<a href>` links to all four key pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions don't conflict with AI-search policy | Clear | Not run | Only `data-nosnippet` on the cookie notice (`app/layout.tsx:15`), which is a scoped choice. No middleware or `headers()` found. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | I read `app/layout.tsx` and all pages. No images, and the links and buttons have text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | `llms.txt` (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. This is optional and isn't scored. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. Not scored. |

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`. It compares real crawler requests against the addresses those crawlers publish.
- **Real status codes and headers:** whether the sitemap URLs return 200, and whether any `X-Robots-Tag` header is added outside the repository. A live scan would confirm both.
- **`/blog` content:** the posts come from `/api/posts`, and there is no API route in this repository. A live check would show how much of the page crawlers actually see.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find the site. `geo.config.json` says `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- `/thank-you` is meant to be `noindex`.
- `https://www.ledger.example` is the right origin, taken from `geo.config.json`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
